name: Cursor
tagline: A VS Code fork rebuilt from the ground up around AI-driven coding.
tldr: Cursor is a standalone code editor (forked from VS Code) with AI autocomplete, chat, and multi-file agent features built directly into the core editor rather than bolted on as an extension.
Best for developers who want deep, editor-native AI assistance including large refactors, multi-file edits, and autonomous 'agent' coding sessions.

Uses a credit-based billing system (since mid-2025) where each paid plan includes a spendable credit pool; an 'Auto' mode is unlimited on paid plans while manually picking frontier models like Claude or GPT burns credits faster.
Backed by major funding rounds and reportedly surpassed $2B in annualized revenue in 2026, making it one of the fastest-growing developer tools ever.
Competes directly with GitHub Copilot and Anthropic's Claude Code, with community debate centered on whether its pricing is worth it versus alternatives.

plans.name: Hobby
plans.notes: Limited agent requests and Tab completions; no credit card required

plans.name: Pro
plans.notes: Extended agent limits, frontier model access, MCPs, cloud agents, Bugbot usage-based add-on

plans.name: Ultra
plans.notes: ~20x the usage credits of Pro; priority access to new features

plans.name: Teams
plans.notes: Centralized billing/admin, team marketplace, Bugbot, shared cloud agents, SAML/OIDC SSO

plans.name: Enterprise
plans.notes: Pooled usage, SCIM, access controls, audit logs, priority support

pros: Deep, editor-native integration makes multi-file agentic edits feel faster than extension-based tools
Fast-moving product with frequent, well-received feature releases (e.g. Composer, Cursor 2.0/3.0 agent interface)
Strong diff/review UI makes it easy to see and accept AI-proposed changes at a glance
Access to multiple frontier models (Claude, GPT, Grok) from one interface
cons: Credit-based pricing can get expensive fast for heavy users who frequently invoke premium/frontier models
Some users report the editor is noticeably heavier on CPU/RAM than plain VS Code despite being a fork of it
Pricing model changed significantly in 2025, and some users were surprised by usage-based overage costs
Power users doing constant large refactors say the monthly request/credit pool runs out before the billing cycle ends

sentiment.quote: Just setup my team with Cursor. They actually got back to me on an enterprise plan (Claude keeps ignoring me).
I stopped using Cursor because of how terribly optimised it is (worse than VSCode despite being a fork).
It's my primary. Claude Code for personal stuff on the weekends. I really just prefer the GUI of having the changes easily highlighted.

bestFor: Developers who want AI woven directly into the editor rather than as a plugin
Teams doing large, multi-file refactors or agentic coding sessions
Users who want a choice of frontier models (Claude, GPT, Grok) in one place
Startups needing responsive enterprise support for AI coding tooling
hotTake: Cursor reportedly crossed $2B in annualized revenue in 2026, but its credit-based pricing means the $20/mo sticker price is really just the floor, not the ceiling.
